title.en: Acids and bases and their reactions

text.en: Lemon is sour and soap feels slippery. Sour things are acids and slippery things are bases. We use indicators to tell them apart without tasting.

Acids turn blue litmus red; bases turn red litmus blue. Phenolphthalein is colourless in acids and pink in bases. Methyl orange is red in acids and yellow in bases.
Acid + metal gives salt + hydrogen gas, for example Zn + 2HCl gives ZnCl2 + H2. The gas burns with a pop sound.
Acid + metal carbonate or hydrogencarbonate gives salt + water + carbon dioxide. CO2 turns lime water milky.
Acid + base gives salt + water. This is a neutralisation reaction: NaOH + HCl gives NaCl + H2O.
Metal oxides are basic oxides and react with acids to give salt and water. Non-metal oxides are acidic and react with bases.
An acid gives H+ ions in water; a base gives OH- ions. Bases soluble in water are called alkalis.
Dilute an acid by adding the acid to water, never water to acid, because the process releases a lot of heat.
All acids give hydrogen ions only in the presence of water; dry HCl does not turn blue litmus red.

prompt.en: What are the main reactions of acids and bases?

points.en: Acid + metal gives salt + H2; acid + carbonate gives salt + water + CO2; acid + base gives salt + water.
Acids give H+ and bases give OH- in water.
